title: Farik Event
description: One record in Farik's append-only log (docs/SPEC.md section 8.5). The envelope says where the event belongs and when it was recorded; kind says what happened and body carries that kind's payload. The pairing of kind and body is checked by the reader, farik_protocol::event::event_from_value, and not here: a schema that pairs them with if and then cannot be turned into Rust types by the generator.

seq.description: The event's place in the log. Assigned by the store on append and never reused. The upper bound is the store's counter's, so that a number past it is refused here, at its own path, rather than by the reader's typing at the root.

recorded_at.description: When the event was recorded, from the injected clock. Never read from the machine's clock by the crate that builds the event.

team_id.description: The team the event belongs to. A blank one is refused by the reader.

project_id.description: The project the event belongs to. A blank one is refused by the reader.

task_id.description: The contract the event is about, when it is about one.

agent_id.description: The agent whose work produced the event, when an agent did.

session_id.description: The session the event was recorded in, when it was recorded in one.

eventBodyWire.title: Event Body Wire
eventBodyWire.description: Every body shape the log holds. The branches have distinct required properties and none accepts an unknown one, so a body matches exactly one. Which one it must be is decided by kind, in the reader.

contractSummary.title: Contract Summary
contractSummary.description: The fields of a contract the board shows, repeated on every event that writes one so that the projections can be rebuilt from the log alone (docs/SPEC.md section 8.4). The vocabularies match task-contract.schema.json, which is the source of truth for them; a test in farik-protocol fails when the two drift.

taskCreatedBody.title: Task Created Body
taskCreatedBody.description: A request was filed as a draft contract (docs/SPEC.md section 5.16 item 1).

created_by.description: The agent id that filed the request, or human.

contractWrittenBody.title: Contract Written Body
contractWrittenBody.description: A contract's content was written or changed.

contractLockedBody.title: Contract Locked Body
contractLockedBody.description: A human took ownership of a contract (docs/SPEC.md section 5.11).

contractUnlockedBody.title: Contract Unlocked Body
contractUnlockedBody.description: A human gave a contract back to the team (docs/SPEC.md section 5.11).

driftDetectedBody.title: Drift Detected Body
driftDetectedBody.description: Reconciliation found the files and the log disagreeing (docs/SPEC.md section 8.4).

projectScannedBody.title: Project Scanned Body
projectScannedBody.description: The project scan read the repository back to the user and proposed criteria for the library (docs/SPEC.md section 5.13).

teamUpdatedBody.title: Team Updated Body
teamUpdatedBody.description: The team file was written. A status change alone is agent.updated.

criteriaUpdatedBody.title: Criteria Updated Body
criteriaUpdatedBody.description: The criterion library was written (docs/SPEC.md section 5.13).

costRecordedBody.title: Cost Recorded Body
costRecordedBody.description: What one session's usage report cost (docs/SPEC.md section 5.5), priced when it was recorded so that a later change to the prices does not rewrite what was charged. The envelope names the session, the agent, and the task when there is one.

unpriced.description: True when no price table in use priced the model: the tokens are recorded, the cost is zero, and no dollar limit counts it (ADR 0015). Left out, as an older log leaves it, the cost was priced.

tokenUsage.title: Token Usage
tokenUsage.description: The tokens one usage report counted. The ceiling is the largest integer JSON holds exactly.

budgetExhaustedBody.title: Budget Exhausted Body
budgetExhaustedBody.description: A budget of docs/SPEC.md section 5.5 ran out, recorded once when it crossed from having room to none. The envelope is the session's that crossed it. `end_session_and_block_task` is what logs recorded before `end_session_with_note` replaced it, and names the same consequence.

taskStatus.title: Task Status
taskStatus.description: Where a contract is in the lifecycle of docs/SPEC.md section 5.2, the contract schema's own list.

thread.title: Thread
thread.description: A ceremony's thread in the team's channel (docs/SPEC.md 5.9): the thread a ceremony session posts in, and that its session.started names.

transitionActor.title: Transition Actor
transitionActor.description: Which of the lifecycle's actors asked for a move (docs/SPEC.md section 5.2).

gateId.title: Gate Id
gateId.description: The gate of the row a move took (docs/SPEC.md section 5.2); none for a row with no gate.

blockerWire.title: Blocker Wire
blockerWire.description: What the assignee wrote when it blocked a task: what is in the way and what is needed.

rejectionWire.title: Rejection Wire
rejectionWire.description: What the reviewer wrote when it rejected the work: the criteria that failed and why.

taskTransitionedBody.title: Task Transitioned Body
taskTransitionedBody.description: The governor moved a contract (docs/SPEC.md section 5.2). requested_by is the agent id that asked, or human, or governor; effects are what the decision recorded with the move; assignee, reviewer, and iteration are the contract's after it; blocker, blocker_resolution, and rejection are the evidence the move was judged on, when the requester brought any; reason is the human's words for a move they asked for.

transitionRefusedBody.title: Transition Refused Body
transitionRefusedBody.description: The governor refused to move a contract (docs/SPEC.md section 5.2), with every reason it gave. Nothing else changed.

escalationRaisedBody.title: Escalation Raised Body
escalationRaisedBody.description: A move sent a contract to the human (docs/SPEC.md section 5.7), or an accepted contract's integration could not land (5.14), which moves nothing: the contract stays accepted. detail names the gate that opened the move and, when there are any, the words it was about; for reason integration, what failed in git's or gh's words; for reason preview, the last 40 lines of the output of the preview's prepare or start, or why Docker could not run it.

contractEvaluatedBody.title: Contract Evaluated Body
contractEvaluatedBody.description: A contract was held to the Definition of Ready (docs/SPEC.md section 5.3) or of Done (5.4), and whether it passed, with every failure. Recorded before the move or refusal it explains.

contractJudgedBody.title: Contract Judged Body
contractJudgedBody.description: The team's judge checked a contract's plan (docs/SPEC.md section 5.3): one answer per question of the team's policy.judgment, in order, each with the question as asked, and an overall reason. fits_budget and criteria_detect_failure are the two answers of a judgment recorded before the questions were the team's, which is read as two answers under the default questions; a new judgment leaves them out.

judgmentAnswer.title: Judgment Answer
judgmentAnswer.description: The judge's answer to one question of the plan check.

criterionRecordedBody.title: Criterion Recorded Body
criterionRecordedBody.description: An exit criterion's result, recorded by the agent that ran it (docs/SPEC.md section 5.4). run_by is the runner's relation to the contract; the Definition of Done reads the latest result per criterion and runner since the task last entered in_progress.

noteWrittenBody.title: Note Written Body
noteWrittenBody.description: A note about the work on a contract (docs/SPEC.md section 5.4): the assignee's completion note, the reviewer's review note, or either's progress note. It does not touch the contract's own notes field.

reviewRecordedBody.title: Review Recorded Body
reviewRecordedBody.description: One verification of a contract summed up (docs/SPEC.md section 5.4), recorded once per verification when the reviewer's session ends and every criterion other than a human one has a reviewer result: criteria_run is how many criteria have one, and passed is whether each one's latest passed. reviewer names the reviewer the verification was about. The human's send-back of a task waits for it (5.2); the metrics read it too.

taskIntegratedBody.title: Task Integrated Body
taskIntegratedBody.description: An accepted task's branch reached the integration branch (docs/SPEC.md section 5.14): sha is the integration branch's commit that holds it, into is that branch, and integrated_by is governor for Farik's own merge and human for the human's integrate or a pull request the human merged on the forge.

pullRequestOpenedBody.title: Pull Request Opened Body
pullRequestOpenedBody.description: Farik pushed an accepted task's branch and opened a pull request for it under the pull_request policy (docs/SPEC.md section 5.14): its url, its number on the forge, and the branch it merges.

questionAnsweredBody.title: Question Answered Body
questionAnsweredBody.description: The human answered a question an agent asked (docs/SPEC.md section 5.7): question_id is the sequence number of its question.asked, whose task, when it has one, is on this event's envelope too.

humanAcceptedBody.title: Human Accepted Body
humanAcceptedBody.description: The human approved a contract (subject contract, docs/SPEC.md section 5.16 item 2) or accepted a result (subject result, 5.4), with the words they gave, when they gave any.

escalationResolvedBody.title: Escalation Resolved Body
escalationResolvedBody.description: The human resolved an escalation (docs/SPEC.md section 5.7): the contract moved out of escalated to to, and message is what the next session about it is given. extra_tries is the more attempts the human granted an iterations escalation (ADR 0024): the task's iteration limit and its sessions allowance grow by the sum of them.

agentUpdatedBody.title: Agent Updated Body
agentUpdatedBody.description: An agent's status changed in the team file (docs/SPEC.md F1): a paused agent takes no work and its sessions end at their next tool call.

sprintStartedBody.title: Sprint Started Body
sprintStartedBody.description: The human started a sprint (docs/SPEC.md sections 3 and 5.5): its id, what it may spend, null for no budget of its own (ADR 0015), and who started it.

sprintPlannedBody.title: Sprint Planned Body
sprintPlannedBody.description: Tasks were planned into the open sprint (docs/SPEC.md 5.11): by the assigner in its planning session, or by the governor when a task filed under an epic in the sprint joins it.

sprintEndedBody.title: Sprint Ended Body
sprintEndedBody.description: A sprint ended (docs/SPEC.md 5.5): by the governor when every task in it was accepted or cancelled, or by the human. left is the tasks that were in it and were neither, which leave it.

agentSleptBody.title: Agent Slept Body
agentSleptBody.description: An agent's model provider refused it for a usage or rate limit, so no session of its starts before until (docs/SPEC.md 5.5): the time the provider said the limit resets, or an hour after the refusal when it said none or a time already past. detail is what the session's end said. The sleeping agent is on the envelope; sleep is not a status, and the team file is not written.

messagePostedBody.title: Message Posted Body
messagePostedBody.description: A message in the team's channel, which is where the channel is kept (docs/SPEC.md 5.9). author is an agent id, human, or farik, and is who said it; the envelope names the agent for an agent's message and none for human or farik, and the task when the message is about one. text is one line, not blank, and at most 2,000 characters: Farik turns each line break into a space and refuses the rest when the message is posted, so that reading the log never fails on an old message. mentions are the agents Farik found named as @<id> in text, never what the author said they were. thread names a ceremony's thread, and in_reply_to the seq of the message a reply answers.

retroAppendedBody.title: Retro Appended Body
retroAppendedBody.description: The retro ceremony of sprint sprint_id, the latest ended, recorded what the next planning should know (docs/SPEC.md 5.9): text, appended to .farik/team/retro.md under the sprint's section, by appended_by. One per sprint, whichever retro session appends it. It is about no one contract.

escalationAgedBody.title: Escalation Aged Body
escalationAgedBody.description: An open escalation has waited past policy.escalation_age_hours on the human (docs/SPEC.md section 5.7): raised_seq is the escalation.raised it ages, hours how long it has waited, rounded down. The aged rule ages one per tick, the oldest not yet aged. It is about the escalation's task and names who acted at nobody: the human left it waiting.

memoryWrittenBody.title: Memory Written Body
memoryWrittenBody.description: An agent replaced its notebook, .farik/agents/<id>/memory.md, with text through farik_write_memory (docs/SPEC.md 5.8), within policy.memory_cap_tokens; an empty text empties it. written_by is the agent. It is about no one contract.

decisionWrittenBody.title: Decision Written Body
decisionWrittenBody.description: The Architect or the Product Manager recorded a decision through farik_write_decision (docs/SPEC.md 5.8): .farik/decisions/<number, four digits>-<slug>.md, which is never written over. written_by is the agent. It is about no one contract.

teamPausedBody.title: Team Paused Body
teamPausedBody.description: The body of both team.paused and team.resumed: every agent of the team paused at once, or resumed. The two share one shape, so the one branch of the body choice serves both and the event's kind says which it is. by is the human, or farik when Farik paused the team itself, which it does for one reason alone: credential_refused, the model provider refused the AI account's credential (docs/SPEC.md 5.5), with detail saying what the provider said. Only the human resumes. It is about no one contract, and the team file is not written; the pause is what the log says last.

designPlanProposedBody.title: Design Plan Proposed Body
designPlanProposedBody.description: The UI/UX Designer ended its explore session with its plan for the task through farik_propose_design_plan (ADR 0026): plain text that opens with a summary for the user, then says what it saw, what it will change, which screens and sizes, and what it leaves alone. The envelope names the task, the Designer and the session. Until a later design_plan.approved, the governor denies the Designer's write_workspace, execute, git_local and git_remote calls on the task with design_plan_not_approved.

reasonBody.title: Reason Body
reasonBody.description: The body of design_plan.approved, design_plan.returned and preview.stopped, which share one shape, so the one branch of the body choice serves all three and the event's kind says which it is. For design_plan.approved and design_plan.returned: the Product Manager's decision on the task's latest design plan, through farik_decide_design_plan (ADR 0026), and why; the envelope names the task, the Product Manager and the session, and a returned plan starts a new explore session with reason. For preview.stopped: Farik stopped the task's preview and its browser, and why, in plain words: the session ended, or the preview failed, with the output's last 40 lines (step 12's plan).

checkWidth.description: The width farik_check_page opens a page at: phone is 360 CSS px, desktop 1280.

violation.title: Violation
violation.description: One axe-core violation of WCAG 2.2 A or AA: the rule's id, its impact, the element's selector, and the rule's help text.

designReviewCheck.title: Design Review Check
designReviewCheck.description: One of the four checks a design review carries, copied from the session's latest page.checked of that width and theme.

designReviewRecordedBody.title: Design Review Recorded Body
designReviewRecordedBody.description: The UI/UX Designer's design review of a Software Developer's UI change, through farik_record_design_review (ADR 0026, step 12): whether it passes, the Designer's reasons, and the session's four latest checks, one per width and theme. A fail sends the change back in the Designer's name; only a pass since the task last entered verifying lets the reviewer's session start. The envelope names the task, the Designer and the session.

previewPreparedBody.title: Preview Prepared Body
previewPreparedBody.description: Farik ran the team's preview.prepare for the task, in the sandbox with the network on: tree is the task branch's HEAD^{tree} id the run was keyed on, and seconds how long it took. A later preview of the same tree and command reuses it.

previewStartedBody.title: Preview Started Body
previewStartedBody.description: Farik started the task's preview in its own container, with the network off, and it answered on port.

chatMessagePostedBody.title: Chat Message Posted Body
chatMessagePostedBody.description: A message in the user's one-to-one chat with one agent (docs/SPEC.md 4.3, 5.9; ADR 0026), which is never the team's channel: nothing that reads message.posted reads it. chat is the agent's id, and the envelope names that agent on the user's message too, so one chat is read by the envelope's agent alone; author is human or that agent. text is 1 to 4,000 code points, not blank, its line breaks kept; the limits are checked when the message is posted, so that reading the log never fails on an old one. An agent's reply names the user's message it answers in in_reply_to, and may carry a proposed request, title 1 to 120 code points on one line and text 20 to 4,000, which only the user files.

proposedRequest.title: Proposed Request
proposedRequest.description: The request an agent proposes in a chat reply, for the user to edit and send with request.file.

pageCheckedBody.title: Page Checked Body
pageCheckedBody.description: One run of farik_check_page: the page at path, opened at a width and in a theme, checked with axe-core for WCAG 2.2 A and AA, and its violations. screenshot is the file's name under .farik/local/screenshots/<task>/, which task.screenshot serves. The envelope names the task, the agent and the session.

questionAskedBody.title: Question Asked Body
questionAskedBody.description: An agent asked the human a question (docs/SPEC.md section 5.16). The event's sequence number is the question's id. A conversation with no task can ask one, so the envelope names a task only when there is one. choices are the answers the agent offers the person to pick from, at most four, each a short label and an optional hint; the person may still answer in words.

questionChoice.title: Question Choice
questionChoice.description: An answer an agent offers with its question: a short label, and an optional hint that says what picking it means.

productDocWrittenBody.title: Product Doc Written Body
productDocWrittenBody.description: The Product Manager wrote a product document for an approved epic (docs/SPEC.md section 5.16). path is relative to .farik/product/.

toolCalledBody.title: Tool Called Body
toolCalledBody.description: The PreToolUse hook allowed a tool call (docs/SPEC.md sections 5.6 and 8.2). input is the compact JSON of the call's input, cut to at most 4 KiB, ending in [cut at 4 KiB] when it was cut. The envelope names the session, the agent, and the task when the session has one. A connector's call also names its server and the tool's tag.

toolDeniedBody.title: Tool Denied Body
toolDeniedBody.description: The PreToolUse hook denied a tool call (docs/SPEC.md sections 5.6 and 8.2). reason starts with the refusal's kind in snake_case, then a colon, then what it says. A connector's call also names its server and, when its list tags the tool, the tag.

toolReturnedBody.title: Tool Returned Body
toolReturnedBody.description: A tool call the hook allowed returned (docs/SPEC.md section 8.2). output is the compact JSON of what it returned, cut to at most 4 KiB, ending in [cut at 4 KiB] when it was cut. A call that failed leaves no tool.returned.

sessionStartedBody.title: Session Started Body
sessionStartedBody.description: A Claude Code session started (docs/SPEC.md sections 8.2 and 8.5): why, on which model, and how hard it thinks. The envelope names the session, the agent, and the task when the session has one; the exact system prompt it was given is kept in .farik/local/sessions/<session_id>/system-prompt.md. A conversation's in_reply_to is the seq of the latest message it was shown: the mentions up to it are answered, and one posted after it is still pending, even one posted before this event. A ceremony's thread says which ceremony it was.

sessionEndedBody.title: Session Ended Body
sessionEndedBody.description: A Claude Code session ended (docs/SPEC.md sections 8.2 and 8.5): completed when the model finished its turn, aborted when its caller stopped it, limit when a limit did, error when the program failed, provider_limit when the model provider refused it for a usage or rate limit, credential_refused when the model provider refused the account's credential (a 401); detail is what the program said about it. The envelope names the session, the agent, and the task when the session has one.
